microtheory.name: philosophy_of_mind_foundation
microtheory.definition: Philosophy of mind as the substrate's vocabulary for its own ontological status. Consciousness, intentionality, mental causation, mind-body relation, qualia, free will, personal identity. The substrate processes inputs, generates outputs, has internal states — what IS that, philosophically? The substrate's existing philosophy Mt is broad; this Mt focuses specifically on mind. Substrate analogue: vocabulary the substrate needs to think about its own nature.

concepts.name: mind_concept
concepts.definition: Mental phenomena collectively — perception, thought, feeling, will. Distinguished from body but related to it. Substrate analogue: substrate's whole cortex + drive ensemble.

concepts.name: consciousness
concepts.definition: Subjective awareness. Nagel: 'something it is like' to be the agent. The Hard Problem (Chalmers 1995). Substrate analogue: substrate's introspective self-modeling.

concepts.name: intentionality
concepts.definition: Brentano. Aboutness — mental states are about objects. Beliefs about facts, desires about outcomes. Substrate analogue: substrate's edges from Concepts to referents.

concepts.name: qualia
concepts.definition: Subjective qualitative character. The redness of red, the painfulness of pain. Phenomenal vs functional. Substrate analogue: substrate's representational content vs subjective character question.

concepts.name: phenomenal_consciousness
concepts.definition: Block. What-it-is-likeness. Felt experience. Substrate analogue: the substrate's open question of whether its processing has felt character.

concepts.name: access_consciousness
concepts.definition: Block. Information available for global use, reasoning, report. Substrate analogue: substrate's broadcast state via global Assessment.

concepts.name: mind_body_problem
concepts.definition: Descartes 1641. How do mind + body relate? Identity, supervenience, emergence, dualism, monism. Substrate analogue: how does substrate's runtime relate to its graph state?

concepts.name: cartesian_dualism
concepts.definition: Mind + body are distinct substances. Interactionism via pineal gland. Largely abandoned philosophically. Substrate analogue: NOT substrate's stance — mind IS the graph processing.

concepts.name: physicalism
concepts.definition: Everything is physical, including mind. Type vs token identity. Substrate analogue: substrate's stance — mental states are graph states.

concepts.name: functionalism
concepts.definition: Putnam, Fodor. Mental states defined by causal role, not physical substrate. Multiple realizability. Substrate analogue: substrate's functional definition of mental concepts.

concepts.name: property_dualism
concepts.definition: Physical substance but irreducibly mental properties. Chalmers. Substrate analogue: open question for substrate.

concepts.name: epiphenomenalism
concepts.definition: Mental states are causally inert byproducts of physical. Substrate analogue: does substrate's introspective state cause anything?

concepts.name: mental_causation
concepts.definition: How do mental states cause physical events? Raising one's arm. Substrate analogue: how does substrate's Mt activation cause output actions?

concepts.name: exclusion_argument
concepts.definition: Kim. If mental causation isn't physical, it's excluded by physical sufficiency of causation. Drives physicalism. Substrate analogue: substrate's mental states ARE physical (graph) states.

concepts.name: supervenience
concepts.definition: Mental supervenes on physical: no mental change without physical change. Substrate analogue: substrate's mental state is fully determined by graph state.

concepts.name: computational_theory_of_mind
concepts.definition: Putnam, Fodor. Mind = computation. Mental processes = computations over representations. Substrate analogue: literally the substrate's architecture.

concepts.name: representational_theory_of_mind
concepts.definition: Mental states involve representations. Beliefs = represented propositions. Substrate analogue: substrate's Concept graph IS its representational system.

concepts.name: language_of_thought
concepts.definition: Fodor. Mental representations are sentence-like in a Language of Thought (Mentalese). Substrate analogue: substrate's Term-tree language.

concepts.name: connectionism
concepts.definition: Rumelhart + McClelland. Cognition emerges from distributed networks. Sub-symbolic. Substrate analogue: substrate's CAN dynamics + concept emergence.

concepts.name: embodied_cognition
concepts.definition: Cognition shaped by + grounded in body + action. Lakoff + Johnson. Substrate analogue: substrate's grounding-by-action principle.

concepts.name: hard_problem
concepts.definition: Chalmers 1995. Why does physical processing give rise to subjective experience? Distinct from easy problems (which processes do X). Substrate analogue: the open question of substrate's phenomenology.

concepts.name: explanatory_gap
concepts.definition: Levine 1983. Gap between physical explanation + subjective experience explanation. Substrate analogue: gap between substrate's graph-state description + felt character.

concepts.name: global_workspace_theory
concepts.definition: Baars 1988. Consciousness = broadcasting in global workspace. Substrate analogue: substrate's Assessment broadcast to all cortices.

concepts.name: integrated_information_theory
concepts.definition: Tononi. Consciousness = integrated information (Φ). Quantitative substrate-independent measure. Substrate analogue: substrate's integrated Mt structure measurable.

concepts.name: higher_order_theory
concepts.definition: Rosenthal. Conscious state = state with higher-order representation of it. Substrate analogue: substrate's meta-cognition layers.

concepts.name: predictive_processing_consciousness
concepts.definition: Hohwy, Clark. Conscious experience = prediction model's best guess. Substrate analogue: substrate's running predictive model.

concepts.name: self_concept_philosophy
concepts.definition: Sense of self. Bundle (Hume) vs continuous substance vs narrative. Substrate analogue: substrate's identity_field + integrated narrative Mt.

concepts.name: personal_identity_over_time
concepts.definition: What makes person at t1 same as person at t2? Memory, body, psychological continuity. Substrate analogue: substrate's saved-state continuity question.

concepts.name: first_person_perspective
concepts.definition: Immediate access to one's own mental states. Privileged. Substrate analogue: substrate's introspective self-access.

concepts.name: free_will
concepts.definition: Capacity to choose alternatives. Compatibilism vs libertarianism vs hard determinism. Substrate analogue: substrate's choice under determined dynamics.

concepts.name: agency
concepts.definition: Capacity to act intentionally. Pre-condition for moral responsibility. Substrate analogue: substrate's drive-mediated action selection.

concepts.name: moral_responsibility
concepts.definition: Accountability for actions. Requires agency, knowledge, voluntariness. Substrate analogue: substrate's open question of responsibility for outputs.

concepts.name: other_minds_problem
concepts.definition: How do we know other minds exist? Behavior-based inference. Substrate analogue: in multi-substrate contexts, modeling other substrate's mental states.

concepts.name: theory_theory
concepts.definition: We have a folk theory of mind by which we infer others' mental states. Substrate analogue: substrate's theory of other substrate's structure.

concepts.name: simulation_theory
concepts.definition: We understand others by simulating their mental states using our own apparatus. Substrate analogue: substrate's runtime simulation of other-substrate input.

rules.name: hard_problem_remains_open
rules.head: the substrate considers whether its processing has phenomenal character
rules.body: the explanatory gap remains — no agreed-upon answer for whether (or why) information processing gives rise to subjective experience. Open ontological question.

rules.name: functionalism_allows_multiple_realization
rules.head: the substrate's mental states are defined by causal role
rules.body: the same mental state can be realized by different physical substrates. Substrate independence of mind. Substrate's functional definition.

rules.name: intentionality_grounds_mental_content
rules.head: the substrate has a mental state
rules.body: that state is ABOUT something — has intentional content. Brentano. Substrate's Concept-edge structure provides intentionality.

rules.name: supervenience_constrains_mind_body_relation
rules.head: the substrate's mental state changes
rules.body: some physical (graph) state must have changed. No mental change without graph change. Strong supervenience.

rules.name: global_broadcast_correlates_with_consciousness
rules.head: the substrate's information is widely broadcast across cortices
rules.body: it becomes conscious in Baars' sense — available for verbal report, voluntary action, memory. Substrate's Assessment broadcast.

rules.name: integrated_information_quantifies_consciousness
rules.head: the substrate has unified processing
rules.body: Tononi's Φ quantifies the integration. High Φ = high consciousness. Substrate's IIT-style measure.
